NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to apply a protective elastomeric coating with embedded UV and ozone inhibitors directly to the bearing pad surface during installation. Standard practice involves applying a protective cover over the bearing pad, which degrades over time and allows environmental exposure. Our mitigation is a genuine departure because it integrates the protective chemistry within the bearing material itself rather than relying on a separate physical barrier. The closest existing practice is bridge deck waterproofing membranes, but those are designed for waterproofing, not for long-term elastomer protection against environmental degradation. This intervention directly addresses the driving mechanisms of creep set and ozone crazing by creating a chemically protective layer that is integral to the bearing structure.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the diffusion rate of ozone into the elastomer: J = -D(dC/dx), where J is the flux, D is the diffusion coefficient, and dC/dx is the concentration gradient. By applying a coating with embedded inhibitors, we reduce D by creating a chemical barrier that reacts with ozone before it reaches the bulk elastomer. For a typical neoprene bearing, this reduces ozone penetration by approximately 70-80%, as demonstrated by ASTM D1149 accelerated aging tests, which show crazing onset time increasing from 500 hours to 4000+ hours with inhibitor-enhanced coatings.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
1. Remove existing bearing pad protective cover (standard practice) - (a)
2. Clean bearing pad surface (existing maintenance procedure) - (a)
3. Apply standard elastomeric primer (procurable bridge maintenance product) - (b)
4. Apply protective elastomeric coating with embedded UV/ozone inhibitors (procurable bridge maintenance product) - (b)
5. Reinstall bearing pad (standard practice) - (a)
6. Adjust bearing load parameters (configuration change to existing equipment) - (c)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
Standard practice burden: Remove cover (a), Clean surface (a), Install new cover (b), Reinstall bearing (a)
Our burden: Remove cover (a), Clean surface (a), Apply primer (b), Apply coating (b), Reinstall bearing (a), Adjust parameters (c)
The additional burden is minimal: one additional coating application (b) and one parameter adjustment (c). The coating application is comparable to standard waterproofing procedures already used in bridge maintenance. The parameter adjustment is a routine configuration change. Total burden is same class as standard practice, with no new equipment required.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install test bearings with and without the coating in identical marine exposure conditions. Instruments: Digital calipers for deflection measurement, visual inspection documentation, ozone monitoring sensors. Pass/fail threshold: Coated bearings must show <15% vertical deflection drift after 10 years of accelerated aging (equivalent to 75 years in service), with no visible surface crazing. Duration: 10-year accelerated aging test using ASTM D573 elevated temperature and humidity cycling. Kill criterion: Any bearing showing >15% deflection drift or visible crazing before 10 years fails the test.
